summary: Grace S. Fong is a sinologist who studied at McGill University and the University of British Columbia (~1978–1984). She served as a professor at Smith College (~1984–1986) and became associate professor and department chair at McGill around 1989.

Graeme MacQueen (1948–2023) was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Harvard University (~1972–1979) under doctoral supervisor Masatoshi Nagatomi (~1974–1979), and served as a lecturer at McMaster University from around 1977 to 2003.

Grafton Elliot Smith (1871–1937) was an archaeologist and historian. He studied at Sydney Medical School (~1888–1892), the University of Sydney (~1888–1895), and St John's College (~1896–1899), later holding a post at University College London (~1919–1936).

Graham E. Clarke (d. 1998) worked in Tibetology and other fields. He held posts at the Institute of Development Studies and at the University of Oxford, where he was attested as a Senior Member in 1998.
Graham Lock is a scholar of Buddhist studies and linguistics who studied under Hsuan Hua and Saddhaloka Bhikkhu.

Graham Parkes (born 1949) specializes in philosophy and Japanology, earning a Ph.D. from UC Berkeley. He served at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~1979–2008; Emeritus ~2008) and University College Cork (~2008–2013) as professor of philosophy.

Graham Priest (born 1948) works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Educated at Cambridge and the LSE under John Lane Bell, he held posts at Melbourne (Emeritus ~2000), Arche at St Andrews (~2007), and CUNY Graduate Center (Distinguished Professor ~2009).

Graves Chamney Haughton (1788–1849) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Fort William College. He served as Professor at East India Company College (1819–1827) and later co-founded and was secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society (~1831–1832).

Gray Tuttle is a Tibetologist, sinologist, and historian who completed his Ph.D. at Harvard in 2002. At Columbia University, he has served as Associate Professor (attested 2008–2015) and Leila Hadley Luce Professor of Modern Tibetan Studies (attested 2026).

Graziadio Isaia Ascoli (1829–1907) was a linguist and Indologist. He founded the Archivio Glottologico Italiano in 1873 and served as a professor at the Accademia Scientifico-Letteraria di Milano from 1861 to 1902.

Greg Bailey is an Indologist who earned his PhD from the University of Melbourne under J. Durham and Madeleine Biardeau. He was a visiting research fellow at the University of Tübingen (1998) and held posts at La Trobe University.

Gregor Ahn (born 1958) is a religious studies and Iranian/Central Asian studies scholar who studied at Bonn and Copenhagen. He held posts at Münster (1992–1994) and Tartu (1995), before becoming professor at Heidelberg University in 1996.

Gregory Adam Scott works in sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, and was educated at Columbia University. As of 2026, he is attested at the University of Edinburgh and as Senior Lecturer at the University of Manchester.

Gregory Forgues is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a Magister der Philosophie from the University of Vienna under MA supervisor Helmut Tauscher, and studied under Birgit Kellner as well as several traditional teachers.

Gregory Hillis is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who earned an MA at the University of Virginia. He held a post at Virginia (attested 2002) and is attested at UC Santa Barbara in 2026.

Gregory Max Seton is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Naropa, UC Santa Barbara, and Oxford (Wolfson College), completing doctoral work under supervisors Vesna Wallace and Alexis Sanderson.

Gregory Nagy (born 1942) is a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He completed his studies at Indiana University Bloomington (~1958–1962) and Harvard University (~1962–1966), where he later held an academic post starting around 1969.

Gregory P. A. Levine (born 1963) specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and art history. Educated at Oberlin College and Princeton University, he became an associate professor in the Department of History of Art at UC Berkeley around 2005.

Gregory Price Grieve (born 1964) is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned degrees at San Francisco State and Chicago. He held lecturer posts at Chicago and DePaul before becoming Professor and department head at UNC Greensboro.

Gregory Schopen (born 1947) is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. at ANU under Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana. He held posts at Indiana, Texas at Austin, and UCLA (Distinguished Professor Emeritus).
